title: Show routine successful Engram events as compact one-line rows, expandable, while errors, warnings, refusals and action-required stay prominent
outcome: In the session transcript, routine successful Engram events (for example the dispatch card "ENGRAM DISPATCH / Turn admitted") render by default as one compact line that can be expanded to show the full detail. Errors, warnings, refusals and action-required states keep their current prominent rendering. Nothing is hidden: every event stays reachable by expanding it.
acceptance: A routine Engram control card that isRoutineEngramControl classifies renders, collapsed, as a single row carrying its author, its stage and its title ("Turn admitted" or "Turn checkpointed"), plus a toggle and its time. It shows no separate label or heading row and no detail block.

The toggle, and the keyboard, expand it to the full card with all of today's detail. Collapsing returns it to the single row. A manual expansion survives ordinary rerenders of the same card, and an active transcript search shows the full card.

Every card the whitelist does not classify as routine renders exactly as before, prominent and fully expanded with no collapse toggle. This includes errors or a causal failure, degraded, shadow or advisory cards, refusals, deferrals, queued, withheld or ungranted dispatches, an armed repair, directives, a waiting next intent, restart, and unknown values.
The virtualization height estimate for a routine card matches the single-row rendering.
Vitest covers (1)–(4) in EngramControlCard.test.tsx and conversation-virtualization.test.ts, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
